claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
WTaTiVZr is a reduced-activation refractory high-entropy alloy.
The HEA has a chemically heterogeneous and severely distorted lattice relative to pure tungsten.
Severe lattice distortion reduces the effective Peierls barrier relative to pure tungsten.
A reduced Peierls barrier enables activation of multiple slip systems.
Lattice distortion promotes more facile dislocation cross-slip and dynamic recovery.
High-temperature deformation of the HEA is dislocation-mediated.
Cross-slip and dynamic recovery reduce localized dislocation pile-ups.
Reduced dislocation pile-ups delay crack nucleation.
Enhanced dislocation mobility and recovery produce a more homogeneous distribution of plastic strain and greater toughness.
Pure tungsten has more localized and constrained dislocation motion than the HEA under comparable high-temperature loading.
Pure tungsten consequently initiates cracks earlier and has lower ductility and toughness than the HEA.
Relative to pure tungsten, the HEA will have fewer dislocation pile-ups at grain boundaries and more observable cross-slip and dynamic-recovery events.
Relative to pure tungsten, the HEA will sustain more plastic strain before failure and exhibit greater toughness.
The comparison will be performed at approximately 1000°C with matched loading, strain rate, grain size, and initial microstructural state.
Matching grain size and excluding secondary phases or impurities will isolate intrinsic lattice distortion as the cause of any observed differences.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the HEA remains single-phase BCC without significant segregation or precipitation.
The qualitative relationship between lattice distortion and a reduced Peierls barrier is supported by literature.
The quantitative magnitude of the proposed Peierls-barrier reduction in WTaTiVZr is uncertain, and residual microstructural confounding may remain.
Absence of significantly reduced pile-ups and increased cross-slip or recovery in the HEA relative to tungsten would falsify the hypothesis.
